card.statement:
Two $t$-tuples

\[\mc A=(A_1,\dots,A_t),\qquad \mc B=(B_1,\dots,B_t)\]

of $n\times n$ matrices over $\ff$ are

- symmetrically equivalent if
$S\mc AR^T=R\mc AS^T=\mc B$,

- *symmetrically equivalent if
$S\mc AR^*=R\mc AS^*=\mc B$,

- congruent if
$S\mc AS^T=\mc B$, and
*congruent if
$S\mc AS^*=\mc B$

for some nonsingular $S$ and $R$.
card.label: Definition 1

paper.title: Congruence of matrix spaces, matrix tuples, and multilinear maps\footnote{G.R. Belitskii, V. Futorny, M. Muzychuk, V.V. Sergeichuk,l Congruence of matrix spaces, matrix tuples, and multilinear maps, Linear Algebra Appl. 609 (2021) 317-331}
paper.abstract: Two matrix vector spaces $V,W\subset \mathbb C^{n\times n}$ are said to be equivalent if $SVR=W$ for some nonsingular $S$ and $R$. These spaces are congruent if $R=S^T$. We prove that if all matrices in $V$ and $W$ are symmetric, or all matrices in $V$ and $W$ are skew-symmetric, then $V$ and $W$ are congruent if and only if they are equivalent. Let $F: U\times\dots\times U\to V$ and $G: U'\times\dots\times U'\to V'$ be symmetric or skew-symmetric $k$-linear maps over $\mathbb C$. If there exists a set of linear bijections $\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_k:U\to U'$ and $ψ:V\to V'$ that transforms $F$ to $G$, then there exists such a set with $\varphi_1=\dots=\varphi_k$.
